summary: Android: check from inside the app that marketing tracking is working
description:
On iOS, a developer or tester can open a debug screen inside a test build of any app that uses the Martech SDK. It shows whether marketing tracking started correctly since the app was opened: an overall health status with the reason, which marketing services started, the id each service uses for this person, and the events the app tried to send. The event list can be shared straight into a bug report. Developers can get the same information in code or in the logs.

Android has none of this. Today, confirming an Android integration works means waiting for data to appear in each marketing service's dashboard, or asking the SDK's author to read logs.

This epic brings the same tool to the Android SDK. It should report the same things, with the same statuses and reasons, so QA and developers follow one routine on both platforms. Each app team decides where the screen opens from, for example their existing debug menu. iOS and Android both ask the user for permission before marketing tracking fully starts, but in different ways. iOS shows the answer to its tracking permission prompt; the Android screen shows whether its consent step has run.

Sequencing:
- Blocked by MTSDK-104. Those fixes change how the Android SDK starts up, which is what this tool reports on. Building it first means building it twice.
- Android first matches iOS as it is today. iOS is still changing what it reports when startup fails (MTSDK-137, MTSDK-138); that part is added in its own story once those close.
- Needed before MTSDK-53 and MTSDK-57 (integrating and verifying the AI Design Android app), as the iOS tool is for iOS.

Acceptance criteria:
- In an Android test build, a tester can open the debug screen and see whether setup is healthy, waiting for consent, or not healthy, with the reason
- The screen shows which marketing services started
- The screen shows the id each service uses for this person, so a tester can check every service has one
- The screen lists the events the app tried to send, each marked sent, or not sent with the reason, and opens the details of any one
- A tester can share the event list from the screen into a bug report
- For the same situation, the Android and iOS screens show the same status and reason
- The integration guide shows how to add the screen to a test build and keep it out of the build released to the Play Store
